newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metro says 96 sales steady at 62 bln marks.
newsitem.headline: Metro says 96 sales steady at 62 bln marks.

text.p: German retail giant Metro AG said on Wednesday 1996 sales were unchanged at 62 billion marks, after a fourth quarter in which sales rose three percent to 18.745 billion marks.
The company also said it expected profit from ordinary activities of one billion to 1.1 billion marks.
Revenue growth was limited by the sale of more than 200 grocery and consumer stores and a mail-order unit, as well as the acquisition of 27 Bauspar GmbH building supply outlets, Metro said.
Discounting the impact of Bauspar and the units Metro sold off, 1996 sales grew 2.1 percent, the company said.
Weak demand also dampened sales growth, the company said.

"The preliminary group sales of Metro AG were within the range of our expectations," chief executive Klaus Wieglandt said in a statement. "Based on that, we believe profit from ordinary activities will lie within the forecasted range of one billion to 1.1 billion marks."
Bauspar in 1996 generated sales of 297 million marks.
At the beginning of 1996, Metro sold 66 Bolle grocery stores and 142 other consumer outlets to Spar Handels AG. Those stores generated revenue of about one billion marksin 1995.
The Wenz GmbH & Co. mail-order unit sold to Pforzheimer Klingel-Gruppe had sales of 602 million marks in 1995.
